name: e18-4yp-Neuromorphic-NoC-Architecture-for-SNNs
description: This project implements a neuromorphic NoC using RISC-V nodes with custom hardware to simulate spiking neural networks. Tested on an FPGA, it supports up to 1,024 neurons and uses dedicated FIFO buffers for stable, low-power operation. The design combines RISC-V flexibility with hardware acceleration for efficient small-scale SNN applications.

name: e17-4yp-Neuromorphic-NoC-Architecture-for-SNNs
description: This project implements a neuromorphic Network-on-Chip using customized RV32IMF RISC-V cores, a 2D mesh NoC, and neuron bank hardware to accelerate spiking neural networks. It supports event-driven spike communication via custom ISA extensions and AXI interfaces, and is implemented and tested on an FPGA.

name: e16-4yp-Neuromorphic Architecture
description: This project implements a neuromorphic architecture using parallel RISC-V processing elements to model spiking neurons, either individually or virtually grouped. It will also develop encoder and decoder modules to benchmark the system on classical machine learning tasks.

name: Configurable Neuromorphic Accelerator for Embedded Applications
description: This project focuses on developing a configurable neuromorphic accelerator tailored for small-scale, embedded applications. The goal is to establish an end-to-end workflow from software modelling to hardware implementation,  enabling real-time, energy-efficient neuromorphic computation within a complete System-on-Chip (SoC) platform.

name: On-Chip Learning for Spiking Neural Networks
description: This project explores enabling learning directly within neuromorphic hardware by implementing both online and offline learning mechanisms. The research focuses on hardware-based SNN learning algorithms and accelerator optimizations to bring adaptive intelligence closer to the chip.

name: Memory and Power Optimization in Neuromorphic Accelerators
description: This project investigates memory and power optimization techniques for neuromorphic accelerators, addressing one of the key bottlenecks in modern neuromorphic hardware — distributed memory inefficiency and energy constraints.
